# Render a cell plot as an interactive Plotly widget

Builds a [`cell_plot()`](cell_plot.md) recipe and draws it as an
interactive 3D scatter. Node sizes are converted from backend-neutral
relative units to Plotly marker diameters in pixels. Panel grids support
at most 10 rows and 20 columns.

## Usage

``` r
cell_plot_interactive(object)
```

## Arguments

- object:

  A `cell_plot` recipe.

## Value

A Plotly htmlwidget.

## Details

Occlusion follows the scene camera, so markers closer to the current
viewpoint appear in front. The `arrange` and `depth` mappings and
[`cell_coord_rotate()`](cell_coord_rotate.md) are ignored. Markers use
the rendered colors resolved by
[`build_cell_plot()`](build_cell_plot.md), including illumination when
requested, while legends are built from the unilluminated color scale
metadata.

## See also

[`cell_plot()`](cell_plot.md),
[`print.cell_plot()`](print.cell_plot.md),
[`cell_plot_rgl()`](cell_plot_rgl.md)

## Examples

``` r
se <- ReadPNA_Seurat(minimal_pna_pxl_file())
#> ✔ Created a <Seurat> object with 5 cells and 158 targeted surface proteins
se <- LoadCellGraphs(se, cells = colnames(se)[4], verbose = FALSE) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral")
#> ℹ Computing layouts for 1 graphs

cell_graph <- CellGraphs(se)[[4]]

layout_data <- FetchLayoutData(cell_graph, vars = "CD82", layout_method = "spectral_3d")

cell_plot(layout_data, color = CD82) |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```
